text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- One prisoner was shot dead during a prison riot on Thursday in Pravienske, some 70 kms to the west of the captal Vilniuys. Some 300 out of 750 inmates rioted and one was shot dead during an attempt to take the head of the prison hostage.
- The government is determined to fight organised crime and special measures will be taken against financial fraud, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius told a news conference.
- A 12-year-old Klaipeda schoolgirl stabbed her maths teacher to death during a lesson. "I wanted to kill her because I loved her," she said later.
- Lithuanian shares on national stock exchange continue to rise sharply.
- Hermis bank expects a 25 million litas profit in 1996 while the internationally audited results will be known later.
- Bank of Lithuania Governor Reinoldijus Sarkinas believes that the IMF would positively evaluate its monetary policy.

- Foreign investment bank Williams de Broe acquired 23 percent of Rokiskis cheese company. Rokiskis cheese share capital is 18 million litas and a new share emission of global depository receipts (GDRs) is planned.
- Kalnapilis beer brewery doubled its sales to 58 million litas and reported a 11.1 million litas profit in 1996.
- There are two million hectares of forest in Lithuanian and one third of it will be privatised. Now 70 thousand owners restored their ownership rights on 350,000 hectares.
- Commercial LNK TV channel raised its advertising tariffs to 4,600 litas per minute on prime time.
- The Bank of Lithuania approved its monetary policy for coming years and intends to keep fixed litas four to one dollar peg until 1999.
- Lithuania will invite international investment banks to manage country's borrowings abroad. The borrowing limit approved by parliament is $618 million.
